title: A look at other server languages: Python, Go, Java, PHP and C#

videos.script:
The first lesson of this course made a promise about the last one. It said that most of what you would learn here was not about JavaScript, and that you would see it again in every other server language.

{{five}} So this lesson writes one small server six times. In Node, then in Python, Go, Java, PHP and C#. Each one answers a name, says 404 properly, and waits one second on a slow route.

{{ask}} And each one is asked the same three questions. The answers agree. What differs is how each language waits. Node waits with one thread. Python and Java give every request a thread. Go gives it a goroutine. PHP gives it a whole process, and with one process, ten slow requests take ten seconds.

{{compute}} Then the work changes from waiting to computing. Four Python threads count primes no faster than one. Four goroutines are three times faster.

{{port}} And at the end, five of them at once, each told its port by the same variable you used in lesson nine.

{{next}} Then the question this course has been holding back: when to learn the next language, and which.
